description: Object destructuring declares one live name per field
code:
point = {x: 2, y: 5}
{x, y} = point
point.x = 7
[x, y]

description: Renamed destructuring targets read the keys they name
code:
user = {name: "Ada", role: "admin"}
{name: who, role: access} = user
user.role = "owner"
[who, access]

description: Names separated by commas unpack a list by position and stay live
code:
range = [3, 9]
low, high = range
width = high - low
range = [1, 4]
width

description: Destructuring an instance keeps its class-level properties live
code:
class Rect(width, height):
    this.width = width
    this.height = height
$Rect.area = $Rect.width * $Rect.height
box = Rect(2, 3)
{area, width: side} = box
box.width = 4
[area, side]

description: A missing field or position reads null until it exists
code:
config = {mode: "fast"}
{mode, level} = config
word = "a"
first, second = word
config.level = 2
[mode, level, first, second]

description: Why explains a destructured name as its own declaration
Destructuring in a standing branch runs whenever the branch runs
code:
pair = [3, 4]
ready = false
if ready: low, high = pair
ready = true
pair = [6, 8]
[low, high]

description: Destructuring inside a function assigns the state names it does not bind
code:
def area(box):
    {width, height} = box
    return width * height
total = area({width: 2, height: 3})
[total, width, height]
